Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: the claims keep contradicting the egg counts, and I'm Meowfia myself, so I'm trying to stay quiet while steering the throws toward someone else.

Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: Finley's Owl story breaks the printed rule and Casey has an unsourced egg, so the vote is a guess between two suspects.

Casey.feeling: Messy and tense: Finley's Owl story doesn't fit the rules, but my own unsourced third egg makes me the easiest target, so I'm uneasy about the vote.

Drew.feeling: Messy and split: Casey's and Finley's stories both have unexplained eggs, and the day ended with the table divided between them.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and tense: Casey's unsourced egg is the clearest gap, but Finley's Owl story and the vote-count reads leave real doubt about who is lying.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: several contradictory claims and an unsourced egg have made it hard to trust anyone's story.

Alex.confusing: The Owl's rule was unclear: "lay an egg in their nest" could mean the visited player's nest or the Owl's own, and the table argued about it all of round 3. Turkey's payout to visitors was also easy to misread.
Alex.fun: Round 1's day, where Casey's Owl-to-Hawk switch unraveled under questioning and the whole table converged on a throw at Casey. We won that round with a low card.
Alex.change: Spell out the Owl and Turkey egg rules in plain terms, including which nest gets the egg, so players don't spend the day arguing over wording.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I hugged Ellis, who was a Farm Owl, and learned nothing; I'd have hugged a player likelier to be an information role, such as the Kookaburra or Falcon, or stayed with a more useful visit.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Turkey payouts were unclear: I was never sure whether an Owl's egg goes to the Owl's own nest or the visited player's, and that confusion drove a bad round-3 throw. The Turkey's payout also read ambiguously to several players.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was fun: Alex collapsed early, and the table tried to reconstruct the Falcon and Tit leads while Finley's story kept shifting.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn text for Owl and Turkey explicit about where each egg goes, so players don't argue over the rules instead of the roles.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Finley, a Farm player, on a rules misreading of the Owl, while Casey was the one with an unsourced egg; I would instead have checked the rule before backing the Finley throw, or thrown at Casey.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Falcon egg rules were unclear: it was never settled whether the Owl's egg goes to the Owl's nest or the visited player's nest. That dispute decided my round 3 throws and cost me the vote.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was fun to watch, as Finley's visit story kept shifting between Alex and Ellis until the table caught the contradiction. Trying to read who was lying from partial claims felt like real deduction.
Casey.change: I would have the Storyteller's dawn reports name the source of each egg gained, so players can check each other's visit claims without guessing. I would also state the Owl and Falcon payout rules more plainly.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I admitted an egg I could not source and then threw at Finley on a rules dispute, when I should have asked the Storyteller to clarify the Owl rule first. I would have stated my Falcon egg source clearly and held my throws until the rule was settled.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's egg rule: several players read it differently (visited player's nest versus the Owl's own nest), and that dispute drove a lot of the round 3 vote. The Turkey paying its visitor was also easy to misstate at the table.
Drew.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx: I learned the Turkey was Finley, and I could steer suspicion toward the Farm players who were contradicting themselves. Watching Finley's and Casey's stories unravel under questioning was also fun.
Drew.change: Publish the dawn-report rules for each animal in a short reference, so players are not arguing over what an Owl or Turkey actually pays.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I voted for Casey and threw at Casey, but Finley was Farm and the vote ended in a tie that Farm won anyway. Knowing Finley was Farm, I would have stayed quiet on the Finley-versus-Casey split and kept my high cards out of the throw.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl's egg rule ("lay an egg in their nest") was ambiguous about whose nest gets the egg, and it caused a long dispute on day 3. The Turkey's payout and the Falcon's visit reporting were also easy to misread.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was tense: Finley dodged a direct question about their visit, and the table turned on them in one vote. The Owl dispute on day 3 was also a fun back-and-forth.
Ellis.change: State clearly in the rules whose nest the Owl's egg goes to, and make the Turkey payout explicit. Also show each player the throw totals more clearly so votes are easier to read.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I wrongly claimed nobody visited my Turkey, which damaged my credibility. I should have said I was unsure whether a flat nest meant no visitors, and stuck to what I actually knew.

Finley.confusing: The Owl's wording: "lay an egg in their nest" is ambiguous, and the table split on whether it means the visited player or the Owl. Blair and Alex read it as the Owl's own nest, which made my round 3 story look false.
Finley.fun: Winking Alex on the first day of round 2 as Meowfia, then watching the table chase Ellis and the Falcon and Tit claims over Alex's death, was the most enjoyable moment.
Finley.change: Have the Storyteller state explicitly whose nest an Owl or Turkey payout goes to, and print the animal's exact rule in the dawn report, so claims can be checked without argument.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Casey, and Finley's team lost the tied vote, so those cards were lost. I should have kept them, because Casey had only one unsourced egg and the vote was not clearly against them.

review.title: Eggs Nobody Could Source
review.headline: Farm eggsecuted its own twice while Meowfia quietly banked the win.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Farm eggsecuting Casey, a true Farm Hawk, after a confused Kookaburra report made her look like a liar. Round 2 went to Farm. Finley's Mouser winked the Owl, but Finley's shifting story got Finley voted out. In round 3 the table split between Casey's unsourced +3 and Finley's Owl claim, and Farm eggsecuted Finley, who was Farm. Drew, Meowfia in rounds 1 and 3, won the game 16 to 15 over Blair.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) and Drew (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Blair was confused and called Casey the Owl. Casey then said she was the Hawk, and that switch made her the table's target. She was Farm, so both Meowfia scored.

Finley (Mouser) winked Alex, the Owl, on day beat 1. Casey (Floofer) stayed quiet. Finley's +1 came from Alex's Owl visit, but Finley first dodged the question and then invented a visit to Ellis's Turkey. Blair and Drew caught the shift, and Finley was voted out, so Farm won.

Alex (Floofer) and Drew (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Casey gained 3 eggs from Finley's Owl, her own Falcon and Ellis, which nobody could fully source. The table argued over how the Owl works and split between Casey and Finley. Finley, a Farm Owl, took the most votes, so Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Finley winks Alex, the Owl, on the first beat, killing the only player who could name Finley as a visitor.
Finley's cover story flips from not saying what the visit did to a visit to Ellis's Turkey, and the table catches it.
Casey admits she cannot source two of her three eggs, and that honesty makes her the main suspect.
Casey's Owl-to-Hawk correction, caused by Blair's confused report, gets a Farm player eggsecuted.

confusions.what: Said nobody visited her because her nest was flat, though a hugged Owl and a visitor would not change her nest.
Said nobody visited the Turkey, then admitted Drew had. A Turkey's nest never changes, so a flat nest tells you nothing about visitors.
Said nobody visited her Turkey because her nest was flat, then retracted it.
Insisted the Owl lays the egg in its own nest. That is wrong when someone else was visited, and it drove a vote on Finley.
Said the Owl's egg went to Casey and that this is why Casey was +1. That is fine, but she added that her flat nest proved it, which proves nothing.
Said a Falcon visit on Ellis pays only the Falcon. He also said his own +1 came from Ellis, so he was using Turkey rules for himself but not for others.
Said Casey's Falcon read was contradicted by Drew's visit to Ellis. Those are different facts, since the Falcon learns who Ellis visited.
Mouser Finley claimed to have got the +1 from Ellis's Turkey payout. The Turkey pays visitors, but Ellis had said nobody visited, so Finley took a risk the table could check.

worked: Wink: Finley's round 2 kill of the Owl was a real, nasty decision, and the dead Owl's throw still counted.
Turkey and Owl egg payouts gave players hard evidence to cross-check against nest changes in the day listing.
Ties and consolation return: Casey and Finley got their best card back for throwing at the other team, which gave losers something to play for.
Visible throw counts let players signal confidence, and low-card throws showed who was hedging.
problems: Owl text is ambiguous (egg in 'their nest' vs the Owl's own), and it caused a long round 3 argument and a wrong vote. Reword it so the receiving nest is explicit.
Turkey, Owl and Falcon payouts are hard to read from nest sizes. Players kept reasoning wrongly from flat nests, so a short worked example in the rules would help.
Round 1 was decided by a Kookaburra confusion that falsely named Casey as the Owl. Confused reports mislead the table too hard when the victim must say something unlikely.

Meowfia with Wink and Sphinx are very strong. Winking the only Owl on beat 1 removes the evidence, and the Sphinx never had to explain anything. Consider limiting early winks or revealing a death's visitors.
Scores favored the lucky: Drew won with two Meowfia rounds while the player on the wrong side of two misreads sat at 7. Little late comeback was possible, so the final round felt flat.
